fields.v: Prompt Triangle (authors' conceptual model for structuring prompts as requirement artefacts), no version

Prompt treated as a lightweight, evolving requirements artefact with three components: Functionality and Quality (requirement, with quality requirements as measurable acceptance criteria), General Solutions (technologies, paradigms, architectural patterns), Specific Solutions (APIs, UI conventions, parameters, data formats)
Not stated as a flow; prompts iterate and oscillate between the three components (H1: early General Solutions, then Specific Solutions, then Functionality details)
Not stated; validation and verification framed as occurring through iterative refinement of the prompt components
Not run (conceptual; one illustrative prompt example decomposed into the three components)
Not classifiable (prompts as requirement artefacts in conversational/vibe coding; no specification files; authors do not use SDD terms)
N/A (illustrative example: new React weather web app)
None measured; proposed for future experiments: correctness and requirement alignment of generated code (H4)
None measured; proposed: stability of the Functionality component across iterations as a proxy for requirement clarity (H3); consistency of generated code (H4)
N/A (proposed future controlled experiments testing different prompt-structuring guidance; no comparison performed)

No limitations section. Gaps/agenda: corpus of real-world prompts annotated by the Prompt Triangle (e.g. from DevGPT); longitudinal studies of prompt evolution and user factors (H1, H2); controlled experiments on requirement stability and completeness vs code quality (H3, H4); requirements-aware prompting guidelines and IDE/tool support

Printed page numbers 415-416 correspond to PDF pages 1-2. Two-page extended abstract; hypotheses untested. One author from industry (XITASO). No data, replication package or pre-registration. Example in React/JavaScript only
Yes (1): aim and hypotheses H1-H4 clearly stated
Partly (0.5): conceptual model and research agenda outlined; agenda steps only sketched (2 pages)
Yes (1): claims framed as hypotheses to be tested, not as findings
Yes (1): no tool evaluated; authors propose a conceptual model only
